interactions.summary: A student distinguishes human beings from rocks and fire by saying humans can stray from cosmic order, and Jiang accepts the distinction only to restate his deeper question: why did God give that freedom at all?
A student suggests God wants to experience free will from within humans, and Jiang pushes back that God already possesses total freedom and does not need creation for that purpose.

Another student reframes God less as experimenter than judge, but Jiang says the room is overthinking and turns to a parental analogy in which unconditional love is recognized by the fact that the child is genuinely free.

speaker_notes.note: The brief interjection about whether God cares is fragmentary in the ASR, but it functions as a prompt that lets the next student continue the judge model.

claims.claim: A student account under discussion says material things follow a fixed order while humans can stray from it, which is why humans rather than rocks or fire display free will.
Jiang rejects the idea that God grants human freedom because God wants to experience free will through us, insisting that God already has complete freedom as God.
Jiang's positive turn is that the clearest sign of unconditional parental love is that the child can genuinely do what he wants, and he identifies that signal with free will.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang snaps the whole problem into a family image: the proof of love is that the child is free.
signature_moments.source_phrase: You can do whatever you want. Exactly. Free will
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the first compact positive account of why God gives freedom, and it will anchor the rest of the argument.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang tells the class they are overcomplicating the question right before he reduces it to a child-parent signal anyone can feel.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you're overthinking this. It's not that hard
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The move marks a method shift from speculative metaphysics to an intuitive analogical model of divine love.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student uses Dante's idea of cosmic order to distinguish natural things that simply follow their path from humans who can stray and therefore need an account of free will.
Jiang introduces unconditional love through a parental analogy and identifies genuine freedom as the signal that such love is real.

chronology_notes.note: This packet is the hinge from elimination to construction: Jiang still rejects student theories, but by the end he offers the parental-love analogy as the lecture's first durable positive model of free will.

uncertainty_notes.note: The student's judge account is ASR-noisy and rhetorically tangled, but the core proposal is clear: free will is being treated as what makes true judgment possible.
